intended_object: Double negation introduction: a derivation of the schema φ → ¬¬φ in any proof system for minimal propositional logic. Inferred from the name `dni`, the type `𝓢 ⊢ φ ==> ∼∼φ`, and the Hilbert-style supplemental module it sits in.
explanation: In this library a derivation (`𝓢 ⊢ φ`) is data, a term of a Type rather than a Prop, so a derivation scheme has to be written as a `def`. This one encodes the theorem schema φ → ¬¬φ, using `==>` for implication and `∼` for negation. It is stated for an arbitrary formula type with logical connectives and an arbitrary entailment system satisfying `Entailment.Minimal`. Minimal logic is the weakest standard setting in which double negation introduction holds, since it needs neither ex falso nor double negation elimination, so the generality is the natural one. The `DecidableEq F` assumption comes from the section variables and is only used by the finite-context machinery in the proof; it does not restrict the statement in any way that matters. The statement matches the textbook schema exactly. Mathlib has no object-level counterpart: `not_not_intro` is the same fact in Lean's own meta-logic, not in a Hilbert-style system.
